title: Look Back, Look Ahead: Coreference Signals in Pretrained Language Model Attention
content: We investigate whether pairwise attention features improve coreference readout beyond pooled span representations in frozen language models with up to 7B parameters. We train mention-ranking probes on hidden states, attention features, or both. Across 15 decoders from 7 families and 3 encoders, combining the two gives the highest OntoNotes scores with gold mentions; decoder gains over hidden states range from +1.5 to +2.5 CoNLL F1, and most of the gain is lost when attention features are shuffled across pairs. Without target-domain threshold calibration, attention-only probes transfer best to the pronoun benchmarks GAP and WinoBias, although calibration changes their ranking against combined probes. In three models, mean-ablating the heads that the attention probe ranks highest lowers the hidden-state readout even after the probe is retrained, with much smaller effects for heads sampled outside the top 64. A frozen 0.5B model comes within 1.1 F1 of our LoRA baseline. For end-to-end resolution, attention that a span receives from later tokens helps detect mentions belonging to non-singleton coreference chains, raising detection precision at a 90% recall target from 48.1 to 63.5 for Qwen2.5-0.5B. An extension to relation extraction with given entities also benefits from combining the two representations.
